script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan rejects ex-US envoy Khalilzad’s 'baseless' allegations of arming Afghans to fight Taliban.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US military needs ‘urgent revolutionary institutional change’ to prepare for modern war, Petraeus says.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: US military needs ‘urgent revolutionary institutional change’ to prepare for modern war, Petraeus says.
Ret. Army Gen. David Petraeus praised the Pentagon’s new Autonomous Warfare Command but said the U.S. must rapidly prepare for modern autonomous war.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Morgan wants criminal sanctions for defamation.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Morgan wants criminal sanctions for defamation.
Government senator Marlon Morgan has called for the reintroduction of criminal sanctions for defamation in Jamaica. Making his contribution to the State of the Nation Debate in the Upper House on Friday, Morgan took aim at the parliamentary Opposition and those he referred to as their surrogates and supporters on social media, blasting them for tarnishing people’s reputation. He warned that the misinformation and disinformation being peddled by these persons serve to undermine the country’s democracy.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: PATHWAYS MURDER TRIAL | Second JP backs claim Ruddock was not forced to give statement.
A second justice of the peace (JP) on Friday testified that Andre Ruddock voluntarily gave police a statement in which he allegedly confessed to cutting Taneka Gardner’s throat. The witness corroborated earlier testimony from a colleague that Ruddock was not forced, threatened or harmed, nor offered any inducement to give the caution statement, on October 18, 2021 – a day after Gardner was killed in an alleged sacrificial ritual at Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in St James.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: What to know about AI-detected Internet security bug.
AP: The language that’s known as the backbone of the Internet is now subject to what experts describe as one of the most notable vulnerabilities in recent memory. PHP is a widely used general-purpose scripting language that is geared toward web development, and thus, it powers the majority of websites around the world. When the organisation behind the language and the Federal Bureau of Investigations’ cyber division warned Wednesday of significant vulnerabilities in the language, government agencies, corporations and other organisations were sent into a flurry.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan rejects ex-US envoy Khalilzad’s 'baseless' allegations of arming Afghans to fight Taliban.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Pakistan rejects ex-US envoy Khalilzad’s 'baseless' allegations of arming Afghans to fight Taliban.
The information ministry on Saturday rejected former United States envoy Zalmay Khalilzad’s “baseless and misleading allegations” that Pakistan was “arming Afghans to fight the Taliban”. The ministry’s response came a day after Khalilzad, who served as special representative to Afghanistan during the first Trump administration, claimed on X that there were “ many reports that Pakistan is arming Afghans to fight the Taliban in Afghanistan”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: Trump’s threat to strike Iran raises public concerns, congressional questions.
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump has renewed his threat of military action against Iran, raising questions about public support for the war and Congress’s ability to restrain further escalation. With midterm elections approaching on November 3, polls show widespread dissatisfaction with the war, particularly over rising fuel prices and the risk to American troops. Reports of renewed US-Israeli military planning have also raised concerns about possible strikes after the elections. Trump made his latest threat at a rally in Florida on Friday.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Taipei Times, NDTV - Top Stories, just now: Israeli forces displace families, demolish buildings in occupied West Bank's Hebron.
Israeli forces pushed into the occupied West Bank city of Hebron on Saturday and displaced around 250 families, some in the middle of the night, vowing to exact a heavy price for a deadly attack on soldiers. The Palestinian Authority called for international pressure on Israel to protect residents, who said soldiers announced the evacuations over loudspeakers late at night as they packed what they could and left.

Israel’s military launched an operation in the occupied West Bank on Friday it said would last several days and include searches and building demolitions, after gunmen killed two soldiers days ahead of Israeli elections featuring security as a key focus. Taiwan should not rely on a single foreign satellite provider for critical wartime communications, analysts have warned, after sudden restrictions on the use of Elon Musk’s Starlink disrupted Ukrainian drone operations. The episode has renewed debate in Taiwan over the risks of entrusting essential communications to foreign commercial operators whose services could be restricted for political, military or business reasons. Analysts said this was particularly relevant as Taipei was trying to...

North Korean leader Kim Jong-un urged his military to train to become the strongest in the world at a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang, state media said on Saturday. Kim’s call for what he dubbed a “Korean-style military revolution” came the same week Seoul’s military proposed talks to clarify the border after an explosion inside the heavily fortified demilitarised zone (DMZ) further strained inter-Korean ties. Although aircraft wings offer a large surface area, their relatively thin cross-sections leave limited internal space for radar equipment. - Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Haryana student beaten with iron rods; CCTV captures 50 blows in a minute.
Rudra, a BBA student, suffered severe injuries after being attacked by three men following a motorcycle collision. The incident occurred around 7 pm near Hudda Park in Bhiwani district, causing multiple fractures and serious injuries. CCTV footage reportedly shows the assailants attacking Rudra with sticks and an iron rod while he attempted to escape. His family believes the assault was linked to a previous altercation involving his elder brother Dhruv.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: Ludhiana: Assailants chop off man’s hand, hand severed limb to shopkeeper.
Shakti Singh Bhura was attacked brutally by assailants during a visit to his friend's house. The assailants severed his hand and handed it to a grocery shop owner as part of the attack. His friend was also injured during the incident which occurred in the Daba area. The police believe that this violent act resulted from personal enmity between individuals.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1939 LA house at risk from neglect, experts warn.
The Sturges House, an architectural masterpiece by Frank Lloyd Wright completed in 1939, is facing severe preservation challenges. Preservationists warn of significant neglect and deterioration of this Los Angeles landmark. While the property owner asserts millions spent on upkeep, ongoing concerns linger unresolved. Urgent action is needed as preservation groups and city officials scrutinize the potential loss of the structure's iconic cantilever feature.
